Explanatory Notes:

1.

COMM courses at 2000 and above level will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

2.

Students may be required to take pre-requisite courses for courses under specific areas.

3.

Students may take COMM courses outside of their study schemes as their Major elective courses, and the course grades will be included in the calculation of Major GPA.

4.

Any students should have taken at least 36 units of SOCI courses before making official declaration to take the Journalism and Communication as their second major.

5.

Students who pursue a second Major in Sociology can complete COMM1120, SOCI1001 and one Faculty Package course offered by a Programme/Department/School other than SOCI and COMM to satisfy the Faculty Package course requirements of both Major Programmes.

6.

Students who pursue a second major in Sociology can be exempted from taking SOCI2003 by taking COMM2160 as the units earned can be counted towards both Major Programmes.

7.

Students who pursue a second major in Sociology can be exempted from taking SOCI1002, and are required to take another SOCI course to compensate for the units to fulfill the Sociology major requirements.

8.

Student must have taken or registered for at least 21 units of SOCI courses at the last term of attendance before making declaration to take Sociology as their second major.

Explanatory Notes:

 

1.

COMM courses at 2000 and above level as well as those labeled as # will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

2.

Subject to approval by the Major Programmes concerned, students may opt out of the Double Major Programme and register for the 1st Major Programme only. The decision to opt out is irrevocable. Students who have opted out are required to complete and fulfill all graduation requirements by following the study scheme of the 1st Major Programme as a single major. Students should be aware that such decision may result in a delay in graduation because the requirements of the single major study scheme differ from those of the Double Major Programme.

[a]

Students are required to take PSYC2010. Journalism and Communication & Psychology Double Major Programme students who have taken any one of the equivalent statistics courses including DOTE2011, ECON2121, GRMD2102, LING3403, PHPC2015, SEEM2430, SOCI2004, SPED2600, STAT2001 and 2006, STAT2101 and 2102 are exempted from taking PSYC2010, and they are required to take another PSYC course listed under 3(b) Elective Courses (2000 or above level) to compensate for the units.

[b]

Students are required to take PSYC3430. Journalism and Communication & Psychology Double Major Programme students who have taken ENGE3610 or LING3202 will be exempted from taking PSYC3430, and they are required to take another PSYC course listed under 3(b) Elective Courses (2000 or above level) to compensate for the units.

[c]

Students who take 12 units from 3(a) Elective Courses are required to take at least 12 units from 3(b) Elective Courses.

[d]

Students who take 15 units from 3(a) Elective Courses are required to take at least 9 units from 3(b) Elective Courses.

Requirements for admission to the 2nd degree programme

 

1.

For admission to the second degree programme, students should have:

 

i.

obtained admission scores not lower than a score mutually agreed by both the School of Journalism and Communication and the Faculty of Business Administration, and this score should not be lower than the lowest admission scores of the Integrated BBA programme;

 

ii.

fulfilled all graduation requirements of the first degree programme;

 

iii.

obtained a Major GPA of at least 3.0 upon completion of studies of the first degree programme;

 

iv.

taken at least a reasonable number of units (27 units as mutually agreed by both the School of Journalism and Communication and the Faculty of Business Administration) of courses prescribed by the second degree programme while pursuing the first degree programme; and

 

v.

achieved a GPA of at least 3.0 in these second degree programme courses. These second degree programme courses include the mutually recognized courses of the double degree option.

 

 

Interviews will be arranged for all shortlisted candidates. Students who do not satisfy the above requirements may still apply for admission to the second degree programme which has discretion to judge the suitability of the students for studying for the second degree programme through assessments like conducting interview, considering the recommendation from the first degree programme, etc.

 

Upon fulfillment of the requirements of the first degree programme, students of this double degree option can choose to or not to pursue the second degree programme. If a student decides not to pursue the second degree programme but has fulfilled the requirements of the Business minor programme, the student may declare minor in Business in accordance with prevailing procedures.

Study Scheme
Learning Outcomes
 
1

1.

Major Programme:

 

 

Knowledge outcomes

(1)

A solid theoretical and practical basis for studying and analyzing communication phenomena.

(2)

Knowledge of theoretical and practical skills and the ability to apply those skills to convey informational, creative and persuasive messages and address social problems for the common good in local and international contexts.

(3)

Specialized spectrum of knowledge characteristic of the professional areas of advertising and public relations, broadcasting, creative and new media, journalism, or communication studies.

 

Skill outcomes

Generic skill outcomes

(1)

Analytical skills

(2)

Problem solving skills

(3)

Critical thinking

(4)

Interpersonal, social and leadership skills

Specific skill outcomes

(1)

Multimedia production and presentation skills

(2)

Professional and creative writing skills

(3)

Information literacy

 

Value outcomes

(1)

Professional ethics conducive to communicating messages in a truthful, accurate, and fair manner.

(2)

Sociocultural awareness of and concern for contemporary social and media issues.

(3)

Commitment and passion towards professional development, intellectual curiosity and life-long learning.

 

 

2.

Journalism and Communication & Psychology Double Major Programme:

 

 

Upon completion of the Double Major Programme, students will have acquired:

 

Knowledge outcomes:

(1)

foundational knowledge in both psychology and communication studies;

(2)

specialized knowledge of the communication and psychological principles behind user-machine interactions;

(3)

basic understanding of computer coding.

 

Skills outcomes:

(1)

basic skills in media, technology and interface design, including computer coding and use of specific programming language(s);

(2)

the ability to conduct experiments for examining how users interact with media and technologies;

(3)

the ability to conduct research to evaluate user and market responses to media technologies.

 

Values and attitude outcomes:

(1)

an appreciation of how technologies can improve social life via appropriate design from a human-centered perspective;

(2)

an understanding of the possible ethical issues involved in media and technology design and development.

 

 

3.

Journalism and Communication & Sociology Double Major Programme:

 

 

Upon completion of the Double Major Programme, students will have:

 

K = Knowledge outcomes

(1)

gained a breath of knowledge in Sociology, and Journalism and Communication

(2)

developed a high level of critical thinking and analytical reasoning skills through cross-disciplinary training

(3)

expanded and extended intellectual flexibility and diversity

(4)

developed knowledge essential to fostering global and regional sustainable development

(5)

harnessed the synergies between two influential social science disciplines

 

S = Skills outcomes

(1)

developed multiple skills in addressing complex world problems

(2)

acquired the ability to theorize, design and execute social research critically and independently

(3)

acquired the ability to formulate evidence-based responses for policy or professional communication

(4)

mastered informative and persuasive communication and writing skills

(5)

acquired analytical and innovative problem-solving abilities in preparation for Industry 4.0

 

V = Values and attitude outcomes

(1)

worked under the mentoring of senior academics and qualified practitioners

(2)

developed a strong sense of social consciousness, freedom of expression, and social responsibility towards achieving sustainable development

(3)

acquired the ability to instill a strong commitment to professional ethics in communication professions and in conducting social research

(4)

developed autonomy, responsibility and accountability in individual or collaborative work

 

 

4.

Minor Programme:

 

 

Upon the completion of the Minor Programme, students will have demonstrated basic understanding of fundamental issues related to the subject, acquired knowledge of some aspects of the subject with sufficient exposure and at a suitable level to allow further study in this subject or related subjects or to pursue a related career.
